title: Keyboard manager doesn't work for Copilot Key
author: panda667

judgment.rationale: The report gives a direct mapping scenario for the physical Copilot key and includes a diagnostic archive; its expected outcomes are clear. The diagnostic triage comment reports editor-shortcut initialization failures, but does not establish that they cause the key remapping failure, so a maintainer reproduction should precede a fix choice.
evidence: The reporter uses Windows 11 25H2 and PowerToys 0.101.2712.0 and describes a Win+Shift+F23 Copilot-key mapping.
Both an Open URL mapping and a disabled mapping still trigger the Copilot chat window.
A PowerToys diagnostic ZIP is attached; the automated triage summary reports repeated editor-shortcut initialization errors but does not prove the remapping failure path.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the Copilot-key remapping and disable cases, then trace whether Keyboard Manager receives and consumes the F23 chord.

fix_assessment.rationale: No fix attempt is linked. A low-confidence Keyboard Manager event-interception hypothesis is testable, but the attached diagnostic summary does not yet identify the cause.

proposed_fixes.title: Ensure Keyboard Manager handles the physical Copilot-key chord
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The physical Copilot key may launch its OS action before the configured Win+Shift+F23 remapping or disable rule is applied; it is not yet known whether the keyboard hook receives the chord or whether initialization prevents the rule from becoming active.
plan: Reproduce with the reported physical Copilot key and confirm the global mapping is active in Keyboard Manager before each test.
Trace the F23 key event through Keyboard Manager initialization and the remapping/disable handling path to determine whether the chord is received, filtered, or passed to the OS.
If the event is bypassing an applicable Keyboard Manager path, correct that interception point and add regression coverage for both a remapped and disabled Copilot-key chord.
verification: On Windows 11 25H2 with a physical Copilot key, map Win+Shift+F23 to open the reported URL and confirm the Copilot chat no longer opens.
Replace the mapping with a disabled action and confirm the key opens neither the URL nor Copilot chat; verify unrelated F23 shortcuts still work.

confidence.rationale: The symptom and test outcomes are clear, but the diagnostic summary's editor-shortcut errors may be unrelated and no key-event trace identifies where the Copilot action bypasses the mapping.

issue_context.summary: A physical Copilot key continues to open Copilot chat even when Keyboard Manager maps or disables its Win+Shift+F23 chord.
known_information: The reporter states PowerToys 0.101.2712.0 on Windows 11 25H2 and attaches a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP.
The issue body says both an Open URL mapping and a disabled mapping leave the Copilot chat action unchanged.
The automated triage comment reports repeated 'Failed to initialize Keyboard Manager editor shortcut' messages in the archive; that message is not proof of a remapping-hook failure.
Related issue #49227 is closed and concerns Copilot-key remapping in some applications; #44650 concerns a Citrix session and remains open.
inferences: The physical key may trigger an OS-level action before the expected Keyboard Manager mapping is applied.
The available evidence does not show whether the F23 event reaches the remapping hook or whether the editor initialization messages are causally related.
issue_context.analysis: The reporter's two outcomes make this directly testable without requesting another generic log package. The red hypothesis is only a possible event-interception failure; reproduce the exact physical key behavior and trace the event before approving implementation.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body and its sole automated-triage comment, including the attached diagnostic ZIP link and listed related issues.
Checked related issue titles and states: #49227 is closed and #44650 remains open for a Citrix-specific symptom; neither establishes a duplicate of this direct global mapping/disable report.
The owning component is Keyboard Manager under src/modules/keyboardmanager; no current report evidence identifies the failing event-processing symbol.

related_issues.relationship: Closed report of Copilot-key remapping failure in some applications; the current issue reports a global remap and disable action.
Open report limited to a remapped F23 key in a Citrix Workspace session.
Older broad keyboard-shortcuts report; no duplicate relationship established.

actions.label: Reproduce Copilot-key remapping
actions.note: The reporter supplied both a remap and disable outcome; verify event handling before choosing a code change.

reproduce.title: Test Keyboard Manager with the physical Copilot key
prerequisites: A test PC with the physical Copilot key that emits Win+Shift+F23.
Confirm Keyboard Manager is running and the test mapping is active.
steps: Map Win+Shift+F23 to open a known URL and save the mapping.
Press the physical Copilot key from the desktop and from a normal application; record whether the URL opens or Copilot chat appears.
Replace the mapping with a disabled action, save it, and repeat the same key presses.
Inspect the Keyboard Manager diagnostic output for initialization or event-processing failures during each test.
reproduce.expected_result: The URL mapping runs in the first test, and the disabled mapping suppresses both the URL and Copilot chat in the second.
reproduce.actual_to_confirm: Whether the configured mapping is active and whether the physical F23 chord reaches Keyboard Manager before the OS launches Copilot.

status.label: Reproduce Copilot-key mapping
status.detail: The remap and disable outcomes are reported clearly, but the root cause is not established by the editor initialization messages.

next_action.label: Reproduce Copilot-key remapping
